VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` not only misreports missing binaries as available; it also misreports timed-out tools as available. `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")`, but each runner only special-cases `"NOT_FOUND"`. On timeout they return `[]`, and `scan_health()` sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` because the runner returned normally. This masks a failed health scan as a clean scan and directly affects `HealthScan.tools_available` consumed by the insect brain. The same root cause covers both missing-binary and timeout false-availability cases; fix should propagate execution status from runners/_run_tool, not infer availability from “no exception”.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports or multi-file resolution, so fix evaluation can report misleading SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts for fixes that only work in isolation. In `bench/endocrine.py`, the sandbox copies only the target file to `tmpdir` (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit only on that single copied file. For files whose diagnostics depend on sibling modules, package layout, or imports resolved relative to the repo, the patched file is analysed outside its real package context. Evidence: the function docstring promises “sandbox-test proposed fixes” and “does the proposed fix break anything?”, but the implementation evaluates a one-file fragment, not a sandboxed project copy.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the immune pipeline marks fixes as `verified=True` when `evaluate_fixes()` returns SAFE or NEUTRAL. That verified flag feeds the NK bug-closed gate in `immune_agents.py`, which suppresses future findings as duplicates of an already-fixed bug. A false SAFE/NEUTRAL here can therefore silently close a still-broken bug across later rounds. This crosses the endocrine → immune pipeline interface and can produce silently wrong reviewer-facing state, which is HIGH in this PoC.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when evaluating a fix, copy the full relevant source tree (at minimum all `source_paths`, preserving relative paths) into the tempdir, patch only the target file within that copied tree, and run pyright/ruff/bandit/test commands against the copied project context rather than a single orphaned file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` can run the provided `test_cmd` against the real repository instead of the sandbox, so the advertised “no source modification” / sandboxed fix evaluation is not actually enforced for tests. The code sets `cwd=tmpdir` in `_run_tool(test_cmd, ..., cwd=tmpdir)`, but it does not rewrite path arguments inside `test_cmd`. If `test_cmd` contains repo-relative paths such as `bench/tests/` or module targets expecting the repo root, Python/pytest resolves them from the temp directory, not from a copied repo. In the actual integration path shown in `immune_agents.py`, the endocrine evaluator is called with `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", "-x", "-q", "--tb=no", "--no-header", "-q"]`. Because only one patched file is copied into `tmpdir`, those tests either fail to locate the suite or, depending on invocation details/environment, execute against installed/original code instead of the patched sandbox. Either way, test results are not a trustworthy sandbox evaluation of the proposed fix.
FOLLOW: This contaminates `tests_passed` in `FixEvaluation`, which feeds `_compute_fix_verdict()`, which then feeds `verified=True` propagation in the immune pipeline. A fix can be marked SAFE because tests never exercised the patched sandbox, or marked HARMFUL for missing-test-path reasons unrelated to the fix. That causes silent false verification or false rejection of fixes and misguides later duplicate-closure logic in NK. This is an interface bug between endocrine and immune_agents and affects end-to-end correctness of the new fix-evaluation feature.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — stage the test environment inside the sandboxed project copy and rewrite/construct the test command to target that copied tree explicitly; simplest sufficient version: copy all `source_paths` plus the referenced test directory into `tmpdir`, then invoke the same test command with paths rewritten to the copied locations.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can label a fix SAFE even when it introduces new issues in one tool, as long as the summed net issue count across tools is negative. The code computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; if `total_net > 0` verdict is HARMFUL, if `< 0` verdict is SAFE. Example from the implemented logic: reducing pyright issues by 3 while adding 1 Bandit issue yields `total_net = -2`, therefore SAFE, despite introducing a new security issue. This contradicts the function’s own docstring: “SAFE: no new issues introduced”.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the immune pipeline treats SAFE and NEUTRAL as sufficient to set `finding.verified = True`. Under current logic, a fix that adds a new security or lint/type problem can still become verified if it removes more old issues elsewhere. That can incorrectly close bugs and suppress future findings via NK’s bug-closed gate. Because this produces silently wrong fix verdicts rather than just degraded quality, it is HIGH for the PoC’s reviewer-facing trustworthiness.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute harmfulness per tool/category, not by summed net count: if any of `net_type_errors`, `net_ruff_errors`, or `net_bandit_issues` is greater than 0, return HARMFUL; otherwise keep SAFE/NEUTRAL logic for all-nonpositive nets.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.68
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can apply a fix to the wrong file because it matches any path mention by substring containment: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A basename or partial fragment in the description/proposed fix can match multiple source paths; the function returns the first such match. This is especially unsafe because it also searches `finding.proposed_fix`, not just a canonical source location. Evidence is direct from the implementation: there is no uniqueness check and no exact-path preference ordering beyond first incidental match.
FOLLOW: If the wrong file is selected, `evaluate_fix()` will patch and analyse a different file than the one the finding refers to. That produces false UNEVALUABLE/HARMFUL/SAFE verdicts and can again mis-set `verified=True` in the immune pipeline. Since fix verification is supposed to close the immune blind spot, wrong-file targeting turns that feature into a source of silent misclassification.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — restrict matching to unambiguous exact basename or exact relative/absolute path matches against `source_paths`; if multiple candidates match, return `None` and mark the fix UNEVALUABLE instead of choosing the first substring hit.
VERIFIED: TRUE
